proposals.title: Integrated Multi-Modal Domain Discovery
proposals.summary: This analysis emphasizes a robust integration of spatial transcriptomics and high-resolution imaging to delineate tissue domains. It incorporates stringent assay-specific quality control and normalization, followed by advanced dimensionality reduction and the construction of multi-scale spatial neighborhood graphs. By fusing molecular profiles with image segmentation data, the approach uses differential expression analysis to validate marker genes and ensure that both molecular and morphological features coherently define discrete tissue regions.

proposals.title: Scalable Integration with Sensitivity Analysis for Neighbor Definitions
proposals.summary: Focused on efficiency and scalability, this method integrates high-dimensional spatial gene expression with spatial coordinates and large microscopy images. It employs explicit sensitivity analysis to optimize neighbor definitions within spatial graphs and uses iterative clustering to identify cell–cell interactions. The pipeline further validates domain integrity by correlating molecular clusters with morphology obtained through systematic image tiling and segmentation, making it ideal for large, complex datasets.

proposals.title: Robust Clustering and Differential Expression for Cell–Cell Proximity
proposals.summary: This proposal targets the analysis of cell–cell proximity by constructing a parameter-sensitive spatial graph that captures local cellular interactions. After comprehensive quality control and normalization, the pipeline employs robust graph-based clustering and differential expression to uncover distinct cell types and subpopulations. Spatial statistics coupled with image feature extraction are used to validate the proximal enrichment of specific cell types, providing insights into local communication within tissues.

proposals.title: Multi-Scale Spatial Patterning and Autocorrelation Analysis
proposals.summary: Aiming to unravel spatial expression patterns across different scales, this analysis constructs hierarchical spatial graphs with optimized thresholding and sensitivity analyses. It incorporates spatial autocorrelation tests to detect both local and global patterns of gene expression. The approach also correlates multi-resolution imaging features with spatial clusters, offering a detailed view of how micro-scale interactions contribute to overall tissue structure.

proposals.title: Quantitative Morphological Validation of Transcriptomic Domains
proposals.summary: This pipeline integrates high-dimensional transcriptomic data with robust morphological analysis to quantitatively validate spatial domains. It begins with rigorous quality control and dimensionality reduction mapping molecular data onto tissue coordinates. Subsequent image tiling, segmentation, and feature extraction yield quantitative morphological metrics that are correlated with domain-specific gene expression profiles, ensuring that molecular signatures are supported by distinct histological features.

proposals.title: Optimized Graph Thresholding for Spatial Domain Delineation
proposals.summary: Focusing on the optimization of spatial graphs, this method uses systematic threshold tuning and sensitivity analysis to define spatial neighborhoods accurately. It integrates transcriptomic data with precise spatial coordinates to generate a high-fidelity graph representation that informs clustering and differential expression analyses. This refined approach ensures that identified tissue domains are both molecularly distinct and spatially coherent, with validations provided by parallel image-based assessments.

proposals.title: Histological Image and Transcriptomics Fusion for Tissue Organization
proposals.summary: This analysis leverages the strengths of both histological imaging and spatial transcriptomics to uncover nuanced tissue organization. The workflow prioritizes image processing routines such as tiling, segmentation, and feature extraction that are directly synchronized with molecular data clustering. Differential expression analysis and spatial statistical tests are then used to validate how well the molecular domains correspond to the underlying tissue morphology, offering a comprehensive view of tissue architecture.

proposals.title: Multi-Modal Cellular Neighborhood Mapping
proposals.summary: Designed to dissect cell–cell interactions, this proposal combines spatial graphs, clustering, and quantitative image-based metrics to map cellular neighborhoods in detail. It begins with robust quality control and normalization of spatial gene expression before constructing a flexible graph that captures fine-scale cell proximity. The approach leverages differential expression and spatial statistics to analyze neighborhood-specific marker genes and integrates morphology from high-resolution imaging to confirm the structural integrity and functional relevance of identified cellular clusters.

plan.user_request: Coordinate specialist agents to propose exactly 8 computational spatial-omics analyses most likely performed in the hidden paper, using a draft–critique–synthesis workflow that outputs the final proposals as a JSON file.

steps.title: Draft spatial-omics analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to read the provided public background and generate a draft set of eight candidate computational spatial-omics analyses likely used in the hidden paper. Represent these candidates in a machine-readable JSON draft at `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`, allowing for any internal metadata needed for later critique and refinement.
steps.reasoning: An initial, TA+CV-informed proposal set focused on spatial-omics methodology is needed before any critique or consolidation; `spatial_cv_agent` is explicitly required to author this first draft so that the proposals are grounded in spatial modeling, neighborhood definitions, large-image handling, and graph/image representations implied by the background.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 1 must use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent by the benchmark specification, and this agent is specialized for drafting exactly eight spatial analysis proposals with internal TA+CV-style checks.

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Use the Critic agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and evaluate the eight draft analyses for plausibility, coverage of key spatial questions (cell–cell proximity, spatial patterning, tissue organization, morphology–molecule agreement), redundancy, and clarity. Write a structured critique to `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` that identifies strengths, weaknesses, overlaps, and concrete revision suggestions for each draft proposal.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique stage ensures the draft proposals are internally consistent, non-redundant, and well-aligned with the methodological themes of the hidden paper before finalization; capturing this evaluation in `critique.json` provides explicit guidance for how the final set should be refined.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 2 is a review-only critique of the draft proposals, which matches the Critic agent’s role of producing structured critiques without generating new proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis agent to combine `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` into a refined, coherent final set of spatial-omics analyses. Write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly 8 items; each item must include only a `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the proposed analysis, without executing any of the analyses.
steps.reasoning: A final synthesis step is required to apply the Critic’s feedback to the draft proposals and converge on exactly eight polished, non-overlapping candidate analyses; enforcing the specified JSON schema at this step guarantees the benchmark’s output format and cardinality requirements are met.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 3 requires final synthesis of exactly eight polished proposal descriptions into the specified JSON format, which is precisely the Hypothesis agent’s advertised responsibility.

provenance.justification: Existing templates (e.g., paper_hypothesis_generation) assume multi-step workflows including paper retrieval and analysis, which conflict with the user’s constraints (no paper search and exactly three fixed steps with specified agents and file paths). Therefore, a custom three-step plan was constructed to match the benchmark’s TA+CV draft–critique–synthesis structure and artifact requirements.
